checks.name: Long gearing alone does not invent engine power/top speed
Long gearing trades away some launch acceleration
Close gearing improves launch but lowers maximum speed
Powerful engine benefits from longer gearing
Sport brakes alone meet the stock tyre ceiling
checks.detail: Expected current model limitation; no blanket assertion that every purchase improves every metric.

checks.name: Better tyres unlock more of the stock brakes
Sport brakes add a benefit with sport tyres
Road sport tyres improve corner speed and total U-turn run
Road sport tyres do not invent extra engine top speed
Stronger brakes do not meaningfully worsen the low-power U-turn
checks.detail: The initial hypothesis of >0.05 s improvement was falsified in pilots. At this entry speed the potential saving is small; do not force every upgrade to win every course.

checks.name: Stronger brakes improve the matched faster-car U-turn beyond three physics steps
checks.detail: Matched engine/gearing/tyres and driver. This resolution threshold detects an effect; it does not establish satisfying upgrade value.

checks.name: Brake upgrade preserves faster-car corner grip

driverLimitations: Reference-driver times include pursuit, reaction and cornering margins; they are not ideal car-performance ceilings or production AI-skill acceptance.

At stock engine power, sport brakes do not save more than 0.05 s over sport tyres alone through this U-turn. The initial hypothesis of a larger low-power gain was falsified; do not confuse better physical stopping ability with a guaranteed useful lap-time gain on every course.
Matched faster-car brake upgrade saves 0.0417 s on this run. Evaluate that effect across later braking zones, equipment prices and player feedback before calling the upgrade well balanced.
